description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:461-468, 504-529

`SctVerifier::verify_sct_for_cert` (lines 130-156) has a `no_run`
doctest example showing how to wire up a verifier and iterate
SCTs. The other three verify-family methods do not:

- `verify_sct_for_precert` — different signature (two cert
  arguments), no example.
- `verify_inclusion` — Merkle proof verification, no example.
- `verify_sth` — STH signature verification, no example.

`merkle_tree_leaf_for_cert`, `merkle_tree_leaf_for_precert`, and
`merkle_leaf_hash` (the public free functions) also have no doctest
examples — they show the byte layout but not the pipeline of
"parse SCT → build MerkleTreeLeaf → hash → verify_inclusion".

The crate-level rustdoc (lib.rs:38-40) says these helpers "give
consumers the full 'parse SCT → build leaf → hash → verify
inclusion' pipeline", but no single doctest shows the pipeline
running end-to-end.

Recommendation: add a `no_run` doctest to each of:

- `verify_sct_for_precert`
- `verify_inclusion`
- `verify_sth`
- The crate-level rustdoc, showing the full
  "parse → leaf-build → hash → inclusion → STH" pipeline

The CT verification pipeline is novel enough (most Rust devs have
not touched RFC 6962 internals) that a worked example is the
difference between "I can use this in 20 minutes" and "I need to
read the spec for two hours first".

Priority P3 because the methods are correct and the surrounding
docs explain the wire format; this is ergonomic documentation, not
contract repair.
title: verify_sth and verify_inclusion lack rustdoc examples — only verify_sct_for_cert has one
